newsitem.title: USA: Last minute problems hold up U.S. budget accord.
newsitem.headline: Last minute problems hold up U.S. budget accord.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Friday that "a last-minute glitch" stood in the way of final agreement on a five-year balanced budget, but talks between the White House and Republican congressional leaders continued.
"There is not a deal. We thought we were close. There is a last-minute glitch," Lott spokeswoman Susan Irby told reporters standing outside Lott's office in the Capitol.
Irby declined to specify the problems blocking finishing touches on the plan to reduce the deficit to zero by 2002.
Earlier, White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles told reporters differences over possible tax cuts were "minor."

But a House Republican source said party leaders were resisting Clinton administration requests for additional new spending beyond what had been agreed to on Thursday. "If this thing falls apart it's because the White House wants more spending," said this source, who asked not to be identified.

The proposal would cut taxes by $135 billion over five years by providing a child-care tax credit, a capital gains tax-rate cut, an education tax credit, and a more favourable formula for figuring inheritance taxes. Tax increases of $50 billion would partially offset the cost of the tax cut. The proposal reduces spending in health care, domestic and defence programmes, and adds money for some of President Bill Clinton's initiatives in education and the environment.
